title: How Damon Chen grew Testimonial to ~$200K ARR solo: niche product, customer-led roadmap, build in public
summary: Damon Chen explains how he quit Cisco and took Testimonial from $1K MRR to about $16K MRR as a solo founder. He covers validating with a lifetime deal, narrowing the target customer, letting customers drive the roadmap, asking for testimonials at peak excitement, and handling churn.

principles.text: Build what your customers ask for; happy customers feed acquisition.
principles.quote: my strategy my core strategy is always you know build stuff that my customers want

principles.text: As a solo developer, start with a simple niche product, not a sprawling tool you can't sell.
principles.quote: instead of you know you build a crm with uh you know hundreds of integrations how are you going to sell right and you have no marketing guys and you just by yourself

principles.text: Ask for testimonials right after a customer is delighted, not on a calendar schedule.
principles.quote: the customer will be more likely to give you a testimonial when their you know excitement is at a big level

principles.text: Don't ship one-off requests; hold a feature until multiple customers ask or it clearly affects revenue.
principles.quote: if some if a feature is asked by you know a customer which really you know has nobody else asked for it and i always put it on hold until you know more similar uh request comes in

principles.text: Check who actually pays and stays, then retarget; price-sensitive solo influencers churned, so he shifted to agencies and SMBs.
principles.quote: later that i think oh you know influencers may not be my target audience

principles.text: Building in public creates a flywheel: shipping customer-requested features gives you content, and content brings customers.
principles.quote: i keep uh getting more content to share and that brings me more uh you know customers
